summary:
Hygieia is an offline-first deep-space crew health monitoring application built for missions where communication delays with Earth can reach 44 minutes.

We developed a full-stack platform (FastAPI, scikit-learn, React, and Three.js) featuring a mission replay engine that scores 14 physiological, psychological, and environmental metrics every six hours against NASA’s five spaceflight hazards: Radiation, Isolation, Distance from Earth, Gravity Fields, and Closed Environments. Hygieia translates complex clinical data into two tailored interfaces: an Astronaut View, which minimizes cognitive load with one plain status (Normal, Watch, or Critical), an interactive 3D body-system map, and a single preventive action; and a Doctor View, which ranks crew triage and displays full clinical countermeasures.

Hygieia addresses the challenge of autonomous space healthcare by providing onboard, zero-network decision support—using local-first storage that automatically syncs to MongoDB Atlas when connectivity returns. As humanity prepares for multi-year Mars missions, crews cannot wait for ground control during emergencies; catching subtle health drift at the Watch stage stops minor issues from escalating into critical crises.
details:
What Does It Do and How Does It Work? Our team built Hygieia, an offline-first crew health monitor designed for deep-space missions where round-trip communication delays with Earth can reach up to 44 minutes. Every six hours—four times per mission day—our system evaluates 14 daily health and cabin measurements, including heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, sleep duration, reaction time, cabin carbon dioxide, and radiation exposure, comparing them against each astronaut's preflight baseline and recent health trends.

A trained machine learning model scores every 6-hour health snapshot against NASA's five hazards of human spaceflight (Space Radiation, Isolation and Confinement, Distance from Earth, Gravity Fields, and Hostile/Closed Environments), translating complex data into three simple levels: Normal, Watch, or Critical.

We designed two tailored experiences inside a single application:

  • Astronaut View: Cuts through medical clutter to display one clear overall status, a single plain-language action to take next (such as "Plan at least 7 hours of sleep tonight" or "Enter storm shelter"), an interactive 3D body-system map, and a one-tap Send Alert button.
  • Doctor View (Crew Medical Officer): Prioritizes the sickest crew members at the top for rapid triage, displays all recommended countermeasures per hazard, and tracks alert acknowledgments.

To demonstrate the platform in action, we built a mission playback feature that steps through 1,095 days of simulated six-person mission data (26,280 readings), allowing crews and judges to inspect real spaceflight emergencies such as solar particle events, carbon dioxide spikes, and severe sleep loss.

What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Complete Offline Independence: All health records save locally on board first so the crew never depends on a live Earth link, automatically syncing with cloud storage whenever a connection is available.
  • Prevention of Alert Fatigue: Critical hazards trigger immediate alerts, while Watch states require two consecutive readings before raising an alarm—filtering out brief, harmless fluctuations.
  • Accessible Spacecraft Design: Every health status combines a clear word, a distinct geometric shape, and a color across three cabin lighting themes (Deep Slate, True Black for night shifts, and Paper).

What Is the Intended Impact? As humanity ventures back to the Moon and onward to Mars, crews cannot wait nearly an hour for ground control to guide urgent medical decisions. Hygieia bridges this autonomy gap by catching subtle physical, psychological, and environmental drift at the Watch stage with early preventive actions before issues escalate into Critical emergencies.

Tools, Languages, and Software Used

  • Backend & Machine Learning: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Uvicorn, scikit-learn (1.7.1), and pytest (39 automated tests).
  • Frontend & 3D Graphics: React, Vite, Material UI (MUI), MUI X Charts, and three.js / @react-three/fiber (with an automatic 2D SVG fallback).
  • Data, Streaming & Design: Local JSON storage, MongoDB Atlas, Server-Sent Events (SSE), Figma, Canva, Photoshop, and Git.

How Is Our Project Creative? Instead of relying on static mockups, we created a live Scenario Bar that lets users jump directly into realistic multi-hazard emergencies within a three-year mission timeline. We also built a lightweight 3D human body map that runs completely offline without heavy external files, alongside a plain-language translation layer that turns dense clinical protocols into calm, actionable guidance for stressed crew members.

Factors Our Team Considered We placed scientific honesty at the center of our design—keeping live sensor scoring locked until a future model can verify multi-day rolling trends, avoiding misleading confidence scores, and clearly labeling every result as "flagged for review" rather than a medical diagnosis. We also designed around real spaceflight human factors (eye-friendly dark themes, reduced-motion accessibility, and human-in-the-loop medical sign-offs) and seamless recovery if communication links drop.
